summary: Carbon County, WY lookout built 1949 on Slash Ridge and moved to the Grand Encampment Museum in 1986; listed standing there; climbing status not confirmed.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (administered the original Slash Ridge site)

access.note: Museum open to visitors (summer Tuesday to Saturday 9 to 5, Sunday noon to 4; winter most weekdays 10 to 4, call first); tower in the museum complex per a visitor tip; whether it can be climbed is not confirmed

events.note: Built 1949 as a 50-foot all-steel live-in tower that replaced the Barrett Ridge lookout
Taken out of service in the 1970s when the Forest Service moved to aerial detection; no exact year given
Moved to the Grand Encampment Museum in 1986 per the register; other sources give no year
Register entry US 2105, WY 7 dated January 1, 2026, nominated by Dixie Boyle

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest; firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts say Medicine Bow National Forest. The story does not name the forest.
The register gives 9,574 ft (2,918 m) for the original site; firelookout.com gives 9567 feet. The story gives no elevation.

notes_for_editor: Museum hours and the tower's presence at the museum come from undated tourism and visitor-tip pages; confirm with the museum (gemuseum.com) before publishing. Climbing status is not confirmed. Height 15.2 m converts the 50-foot figure from firelookout.com. The 1986 move year comes from the register alone. The record's agency is null; the Forest Service entry refers to the original site.
